What does being "good" mean to you? It's a loaded question I know but, that is where you start this journey. Is it what makes people happy? Is it what makes you happy? Is good what is fair? Is to be good to be moral? Is good the needs of the whole over the individual? Is good an absolute state of being or a sliding scale? This is some meaning of life next level shit, so don't hate yourself if you take 50 years to find an answer you are satisfied with.

The next 50 years starts now right? So let's go. Good means to do that which brings the least harm and maximum good to yourself and the world around you. That sound awfully utilitarian so let's add that it should also make you happy in ways that are intangible and there should be a balance between the utilitarian and romantic/spiritual satisfaction that goodness brings.

I like to think that goodness is what makes the majority of people happy. I don't know if what I understand to be good makes me happy all the time of even if happiness should be my goal, because sometimes that which is good will require the hardships and paind and displeasure that can only be described as bad, which is the opposite of good. So goodness and badness are linked and inseparable. Morality and fairness are sliding scales that alter according to the situation in a healthy person because that is how we make sense of ever changing circumstance.

That's some of those tackled now poke holes at will and we'll both be better for it.
In your thoughts how do you deal with causality and the cycle of good and bad feeding into each other?

I don't know, It's one of the greater mysteries that I have to say I rely on religious and moral and rational evidence and experience to rationalize.

Do you have any thoughts on that?

For me, the human view of good and bad is too narrow. An event does not produce a chain of either wholly good or wholly bad events. Good, bad, and neutral chains of events propagate into the future. For instance, recently, I found a hundred dollars (+1 good) balled up in a receipt that someone lost (-1 good) but I use that hundred dollars to buy a used printer from a small business (+1 good). The story of this $100 will continue on affecting people in various ways. Unless I can see the final outcome, I won't ever know if the original loss of this money was a net good or net bad event. Also, I don't know anything about the chain events surrounding this bill before it came into my possession. Good and bad are unknowable absolutes for me. So I treat everyone and everything like it has the potential for goodness.

This is where faith comes into it. If you believe as you say that everyone and everything is potentially good and let that influence your behaviour, aren't you being naive about the inevitable negative actors or actors. Why not let the world show you it's relative goodness or badness and let that inform your interactions. That puts the onus on you to behave in the maximum "good" way you know how. That means that you can influence the parts of the world you have control over to be +1 good insofar as you can. That means that you will interact with more goodness than negative influences.

So what happens when you fail and don't treat everyone and everything in a "+1 good" manner and or you are proven wrong in your initial assumption about their potential goodness? Why must you suffer that badness?

I have faith that the universe will do everything to perpetuate it's own existence. I have faith in my own abilities to take advantage of situations I find favorable to my goals as they arise. I consciously create good and bad in the world. Being good is not the reason I exist although sometimes It suits me to be good just as sometimes it suits me to be bad. Once again, I don't know if anything is ultimately good or bad, there are only outcomes that further my goals and outcomes that don't and I am at peace with this fact.

I don't think any creature is entitled to experience only goodness so I feel no burden to always help others achieve their ideal outcome and I do not take it personally when bad stuff happens to me because random shit does happen in spite of my efforts to create outcomes I like. Universe is fair like that, no one is immune to random events.
